stem: A postoperative client is taking shallow breaths because movement of the abdominal incision is painful. Which nursing intervention best supports prevention of postoperative pulmonary complications?

options.A: Encourage prescribed pain-control measures, then coach deep breathing and coughing while the client splints the incision as appropriate
options.B: Ask the client to avoid coughing and deep breathing until the incision is pain free so the wound is not stressed
options.C: Keep the client on strict bed rest because mobility and deeper respirations increase the risk of atelectasis
options.D: Use leg exercises as the primary intervention for lung expansion and secretion clearance

rationale: Postoperative pulmonary care includes adequate pain control plus deep breathing/coughing and other prescribed lung-expansion measures. Splinting can reduce incisional discomfort during coughing. These measures promote ventilation and secretion clearance and reduce atelectasis risk; they complement, rather than replace, mobilization and other prescribed prophylaxis.
educational_objective: Use pain control and coached pulmonary-hygiene measures to improve lung expansion and secretion clearance after surgery.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf
source_locator: Table 2.5b Routine Postoperative Nursing Interventions — respiratory care: teach coughing/deep breathing or prescribed incentive spirometry; teach splinting; ambulate to promote ventilation and secretion removal
source_claim_supported: Postoperative respiratory care uses lung-expansion/secretion-clearance measures, with splinting and pain management supporting participation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — comfort measures, mobility and postoperative care
blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — postoperative pulmonary hygiene and comfort
correction_summary: Replaced a simple purpose-definition item and implausible distractors with an applied postoperative scenario integrating pain control, splinting, deep breathing and coughing. Removed any guarantee that these measures alone prevent pneumonia.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Pain control, deep breathing/coughing, splinting and secretion-clearance rationale supported.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; avoiding pulmonary hygiene promotes secretion retention/atelectasis.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; unnecessary bed rest worsens pulmonary and thrombotic risk.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; leg exercises address mobility/venous stasis, not primary lung expansion.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A directly addresses shallow breathing and secretion clearance.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices are postoperative nursing strategies.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked incision stress, cough contraindications, abdominal surgery context, pain management and overlap with incentive spirometry; no unresolved conflict.
